clinician.final_diagnosis: grade III hemangiopericytoma according to the WHO 2016 classification
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old man presented with increasingly intense headaches. Initial brain imaging revealed a left temporo-parieto-occipital intraaxial tumor, initially suggestive of a high-grade glial tumor. The patient underwent complete surgical excision of the tumor. Pathological examination with immunohistochemical study confirmed the diagnosis of a grade III hemangiopericytoma according to the WHO 2016 classification. Postoperatively, the patient received adjuvant radiotherapy (VMAT technique, 54Gy) with good tolerance. Control imaging 3 months after the end of radiotherapy showed no peculiarity.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with increasingly intense headaches resistant to usual analgesics.
Initial imaging (MRI/CT) revealed a left temporo-parieto-occipital intraaxial tumor process, initially evoking a high-grade glial tumor.
Complete excision of the tumor was performed.
Pathological examination with immunohistochemical study confirmed a grade III hemangiopericytoma according to the WHO 2016 classification.
Adjuvant radiotherapy with a VMAT technique at a total dose of 54Gy was administered with good tolerance.
Control imaging 3 months after the end of radiotherapy showed no peculiarity.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Initial imaging appearance evoked a high-grade glial tumor (E001), but definitive histopathological examination with immunohistochemistry confirmed hemangiopericytoma (E002).
